newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong inks border agreement with China.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong inks border agreement with China.

text.p: Hong Kong and China signed an agreement on Thursday officially demarcating their border in preparation for the transfer of sovereignty in 12 days time.
The 156-year-old British colony is reverting to China at midnight on June 30. London and Beijing had agreed on a new administrative border for the territory six months ago.
The deal, finally signed in the Chinese city of Shenzhen just across the frontier, will remove a number of anomalies that have made frontier policing difficult for both sides.

Until now China's territorial waters, for example, came up to the shoreline of a section of coast on Hong Kong's largest island Lantau, making it a target for smugglers and illegal immigrants. The boundary has now been moved farther from shore. The agreement also irons out wrinkles along the land border.
The aim was to set out a clear administrative boundary for the entire territory with China's Guangdong province, a Hong Kong government statement said after the signing.
Although China is resuming sovereignty over Hong Kong, it plans to keep the territory separate from the rest of the country as a highly autonomous capitalist region.
